newsitem.title: UK: UK to make BSkyB offer decoder box to others.
newsitem.headline: UK to make BSkyB offer decoder box to others.

text.p: The government will make its proposals for conditional access services for digital television available to Parliament before the Christmas recess, trade minister Ian Taylor said on Thursday.
He said they will, provided Parliament approves them, come into force within 21 days.

"The draft regulations ensure that whoever establishes a population of set top boxes, all broadcasters will be able to gain access on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms," Taylor said in a written parliamentary reply.

Taylor had been asked by Conservative member of parliament Tim Renton what progress he had made in finalising regulations to require British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc to licences its decoder box and other associated digital technology to other broadcasters.
Earlier, BSkyB deputy managing director David Chance told Parliament's National Heritage Committee it had no intention of preventing rival broadcasters from using its technology.
"It is very much our intent to want to encourage use of the system by as many broadcasters as possible. That is the basis of our business -- multi-channel television choice," Chance said.
